reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Qualifying areas and petitions for sanitary districts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 12476; prior revisions 1929, 1919, 1909). Covers areas lying partly inside and partly outside a city of 300,000 or more needing common drainage or sewers for public health, authorizing the city mayor and assembly and/or county commission (both if a city performs county functions) to petition the circuit court(s) for commissioners and voter submission.

headings.title: Petition form, territory description, and suggested district name
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Permits petitions to take the form of a city ordinance or county commission order and requires a general territory description and suggested name for the proposed sanitary district.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (2 subsections) and RSMo 1939/prior revision notes; verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked qualifying areas partly inside and partly outside a city of >=300,000 and petitioning parties (city mayor/assembly and/or county commission, both where city performs county functions) in (1), and ordinance/order petition form, general territory description, and suggested name in (2). Retained both drafted headings.

headings.title: Circuit court appointment of three boundary commissioners
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 12477; prior revisions 1929, 1919, 1909). Authorizes petitioned circuit court(s) to appoint three disinterested persons, including one civil engineer or surveyor, as commissioners to lay out and define proposed sanitary district boundaries.

headings.title: Commissioners' authority to alter boundaries, survey, and map
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Permits commissioners to alter or amend petition boundaries to include efficiently drainable areas or exclude unbenefitted natural drainage areas, with authority to have necessary surveys and maps made.

headings.title: Commissioners' oath, published meeting notice, and venue
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Requires commissioners to qualify by oath, publish meeting notice at least five times in general-circulation newspaper(s) at least twenty days before the meeting, and hold the boundary meeting at the county courthouse or city hall.

headings.title: Presiding commissioner, public hearing, and boundary determination
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history notes. Designates the first-named commissioner to preside, gives residents and real property owners in or adjacent to the proposed district a right to be heard on boundaries, and authorizes a majority of commissioners to fix boundaries after the hearing.

headings.title: Hearing adjournments, commissioner pay, and stenographer-clerk employment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history notes. Authorizes day-to-day adjournments until the hearing concludes, sets archived commissioner compensation at $10 per day of actual service, and permits employing a stenographer and clerk at $5 per day.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (5 subsections) and RSMo 1939/prior revision notes; verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked circuit court appointment of 3 disinterested commissioners (one civil engineer/surveyor) in (1), boundary alteration/survey/map powers in (2), oath, 5-time >=20-day published notice, and courthouse/city hall venue in (3), presiding commissioner, resident/owner hearing right, and majority boundary determination in (4), and day-to-day adjournments plus archived $10/day commissioner and $5/day stenographer-clerk pay in (5). Retained all five drafted headings.

headings.title: Duty to submit district organization to voters
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 12477, A.L. 1978 H.B. 971). Directs the mayor and county commission or courts (retaining archived phrasing 'commission or courts') to submit organization and incorporation of the proposed sanitary district with approved boundaries to voters at an election.

headings.title: Certifying election returns to the secretary of state
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Requires election returns certified under oath by vote receivers and counters to be made to the Missouri secretary of state to ascertain and declare the result.

headings.title: Statutory ballot question form
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 (including continuation ballot text block [b7]) and history notes. Prescribes submitting the question in substantially the form: 'Shall a sanitary drainage district be organized and incorporated?'

headings.title: District organization upon majority voter approval
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history notes. Provides that if a majority of votes cast favor organization, the proposed district is thenceforth deemed an organized sanitary district under chapter 248.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (4 subsections including ballot continuation block [b7]) and 1978 history notes; verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked mayor and 'county commission or courts' [archived wording retained] duty to submit organization to voters in (1), sworn election returns to secretary of state in (2), statutory ballot question form in (3), and majority-vote organization in (4). Retained all four drafted headings.

headings.title: Corporate status, name, seal, and general powers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 12477; prior revisions 1929, 1919, 1909). Establishes the district upon appointment and organization of section 248.070 trustees as a body corporate and politic styled 'The Sanitary District of ______', with power to sue and be sued, contract, hold real and personal property, and adopt a common seal.

headings.title: Judicial notice of organized sanitary districts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Requires all Missouri courts to take judicial notice of the existence of sanitary districts organized under chapter 248.

headings.title: Allocation of preliminary proceeding costs by election outcome
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Assigns all preliminary proceeding costs to the district if the proposition carries; if defeated, assigns court, commissioner, and election costs to the city and county separately under their respective petitions if of independent jurisdiction, or all expenses to the county commission if jurisdiction is single.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (3 subsections) and RSMo 1939/prior revision notes; verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked corporate status/name/powers upon appointment and organization of section 248.070 trustees in (1), statewide judicial notice in (2), and allocation of preliminary proceeding costs to the district if passed, or to independent city/county jurisdictions or single-jurisdiction county commission if defeated, in (3). Retained all three drafted headings.

headings.title: Board of trustees composition, appointment, and president
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 12478; prior revisions 1929, 1919, 1909). Establishes a three-member board appointed respectively by the county commission, the city mayor (with approval of the higher legislative branch), and the circuit court (a reputable civil engineer and drainage expert who serves as board president and executive officer).

headings.title: Court-fixed per diem salaries for trustees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Provides that trustees receive salaries proportioned to actual services rendered, fixed on a per diem basis by the circuit court appointing the third member.

headings.title: Common trustees for overlapping sanitary districts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Permits appointing the same persons as trustees for any or all sanitary districts sharing territory common to the same city and county or counties.

headings.title: Filling trustee vacancies and removal for cause
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history notes. Authorizes each appointing official, county commission, or court to appoint a successor upon death, resignation, removal, or term expiration and to remove its appointee for cause.

headings.title: Initial and subsequent terms subject to section 248.180
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history notes. Sets staggered initial terms (circuit court appointee three years, county commission two years, mayor one year) and subsequent three-year terms, expressly conditioned on the board's potential abolition under section 248.180.

headings.title: Board officers, employees, bonds, and salary cap
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history notes. Authorizes the board to elect a clerk, chief engineer, and attorney, hire and discharge other necessary employees at pleasure, fix compensation and bond requirements, and caps any per-diem-calculated salary at the board president's per diem.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (6 subsections) and RSMo 1939/prior revision notes; verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked 3-trustee appointment (county commission, mayor with upper legislative approval, circuit court civil-engineer president) in (1), court-fixed per diem salaries in (2), common trustees for overlapping districts in (3), vacancy filling and removal for cause by appointing authority in (4), staggered initial and 3-year subsequent terms subject to section 248.180 abolition in (5), and board officers, at-pleasure employees, bonds, and president-per-diem salary cap in (6). Retained all six drafted headings.

headings.title: Surveys, general drainage plan, branch limits, and subdistricts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, history notes (RSMo 1939 § 12482; prior revisions 1929, 1919, 1909 [section symbol omitted before 5693 in source]), and cross-reference notes (70.210–70.320, 64.010–64.295). Covers surveying and mapping natural drainage areas, laying out a general plan of outlets and branches/submains (limiting general-revenue branches to drainage areas of at least 800 acres), open channels with intercepting sewers, and subdividing into subdistricts up to 1,000 acres funded at subdistrict expense under section 248.160.

headings.title: Ordinance adoption, publication, binding effect, and farm-drain exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, history notes, and cross-reference notes. Requires adopting completed district or subdistrict plans by ordinance published in general-circulation newspaper(s), binding all persons, corporations, and municipalities and barring inconsistent or unpermitted drainage work except ordinary farm or agricultural drains.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (2 subsections), history notes (retaining omitted '§' before 1909 5693), and 70.210–70.320/64.010–64.295 cross-references; verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked surveys, general plan, 800-acre general-revenue branch limit, open channels with intercepting sewers, and <=1,000-acre subdistricts under 248.160 in (1), and published ordinance adoption, binding effect, and ordinary farm/agricultural drain exception in (2). Retained both drafted headings.

headings.title: Acquiring private rights-of-way by condemnation, purchase, or gift
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 12483; prior revisions 1929, 1919, 1909). Covers board ordinance calling upon city or county condemnation authority to procure private drainage rights-of-way or easements, alternative acquisition by purchase, gift, or otherwise, and paying proceeding costs and damages from the special drainage fund in the treasury of the city or county where taken property lies.

headings.title: Crossing public ways and parks upon approved plans
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Grants conditional authority to cross or traverse public streets, roads, alleys, parks, or places upon filing a location map and non-interfering work plan (allowing reasonable construction time) subject to approval by the county commission or city mayor.

headings.title: District responsibility for work and ground restoration costs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Requires the sanitary district to bear the entire expense of works and restoration of occupied ground as near as may be to its former condition.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (3 subsections) and RSMo 1939/prior revision notes; verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked private right-of-way acquisition by city/county condemnation, purchase, or gift paid from city/county special drainage fund in (1), conditional public-way/park crossing subject to map/non-interfering plan approval by county commission or mayor in (2), and district responsibility for work and ground restoration costs in (3). Retained all three drafted headings.

headings.title: Competitive bidding over five hundred dollars and exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 12485; prior revisions 1929, 1919, 1909). Requires letting construction contracts exceeding $500 to the lowest responsible bidder (excluding repairs or emergencies requiring prompt attention) after at least twenty days' newspaper publication (and optional contractor papers), reserving board power to reject all bids and readvertise.

headings.title: Contracts for surveys, plans, and work superintendence
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Authorizes board agreements with competent persons, firms, or corporations to prepare needed surveys, maps, and plans and to lay out and superintend chapter construction, limited to one piece or class of work per agreement.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (2 subsections) and RSMo 1939/prior revision notes; verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked competitive bidding >$500 after >=20 days' notice, bid rejection/readvertisement, and repair/emergency exceptions in (1), and survey/plan/superintendence agreements limited to one piece or class of work per contract in (2). Revised (1) to 'Competitive bidding over five hundred dollars and exceptions' so the bidding requirement is not presented as unconditional; retained (2).

headings.title: Uniform special drainage tax levy, cap, and collection
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 12480; prior revisions 1929, 1919, 1909). Requires city authorities and county commissions to levy a board-certified uniform special drainage tax on district lands (excluding opened public streets, roads, and alleys) in addition to general municipal/county limits, capped at one-half of one percent of annual equalized valuation, with no other land exemptions and collection like state and county taxes.

headings.title: Special drainage fund deposit and section 248.140 use
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Directs collected amounts into city and county treasuries credited to 'The Drainage Fund of the Sanitary District of ______', restricted exclusively to paying vouchers drawn under board authority specified in section 248.140.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (2 subsections) and RSMo 1939/prior revision notes; verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked board-certified uniform special drainage tax levied by city/county in addition to general limits (<=0.5% equalized valuation, public ways excluded, no other exemptions, state/county collection) in (1), and deposit into city/county special drainage fund restricted exclusively to section 248.140 board vouchers in (2). Retained both drafted headings.

headings.title: Application to county commission for revenue anticipation bonds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, history notes (RSMo 1939 § 12484; prior revisions 1929, 1919, 1909), and cross-reference notes (108.180–108.210, 108.230, 108.140–108.160). Permits the board, when urgent sanitary construction outstrips section 248.120 means, to apply to the county commission(s) for an order authorizing revenue anticipation bonds, stating purpose, amount, and conditions.

headings.title: County commission bond authorization and statutory limits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, history notes, and cross-reference notes. Grants the county commission discretion to authorize bonds, capped so total outstanding bonds never exceed ten years' anticipated revenue at a one-half of one percent annual levy on current valuation, with terms up to twenty years and interest up to six percent.

headings.title: Annual sinking fund charge against special tax collections
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3, history notes, and cross-reference notes. Requires charging the special tax collection fund first each year with falling-due interest and a proportional share of total outstanding principal (divided by remaining bond years) set apart as a sinking fund for interest and bond payment or purchase.

headings.title: Required bond printing and secretary of state registration
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4, history notes, and cross-reference notes. Requires printing a copy of section 248.130 and the county commission order on the back of chapter bonds and registering the bonds in the Missouri secretary of state's office.

headings.title: State treasury deposit and payment from sinking fund
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5, history notes, and cross-reference notes. Directs annual payment of the sinking fund into the state treasury, with principal and interest paid as for state-payable bonds.

headings.title: City treasury deposit and restricted bond proceeds use
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6, history notes, and cross-reference notes. Requires depositing bond proceeds with the city treasurer as a special fund used solely to pay vouchers for work done or materials furnished in constructing channels, drains, and sewers.

headings.title: Privileged supreme court appeal from bond application action
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7, history notes, and cross-reference notes. Provides for appeals from action of 'the court applied to as above provided' (archival source terminology retaining 'court' from former county court wording where subsections 1, 2, and 4 were updated to 'county commission') to be heard and determined as a privileged case by the Missouri Supreme Court.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (7 subsections), history notes, and 108.180–108.230/108.140–108.160 cross-references; verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked urgent-measure bond application to county commission(s) when 248.120 means are insufficient in (1), discretionary authorization and 10-year/0.5%, 20-year, 6% limits in (2), first-charge annual sinking fund in (3), required back-of-bond printing and secretary of state registration in (4), state treasury sinking-fund deposit/payment in (5), city treasury proceeds deposit restricted to construction vouchers in (6), and privileged Missouri Supreme Court appeal from 'the court applied to as above provided' (explicitly documenting vestigial 'court' wording where (1), (2), and (4) read 'county commission') in (7). Revised (7) to 'Privileged supreme court appeal from bond application action' to avoid ambiguity over the vestigial 'court' reference without silently rewriting the source; retained (1)–(6).

headings.title: Subdistrict sewer construction authority and area-based special assessment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, history notes (RSMo 1939 § 12487; prior revisions 1929, 1919, 1909), and cross-reference notes (140.380, 249.710–249.750). Allocates subdistrict sewer powers (not exceeding 1,000 acres) to section 248.070 trustees across independent jurisdictions or to the single municipality/county when wholly within one jurisdiction, triggered by majority resident taxpayer petition or board of health recommendation, and authorizes uniform special tax assessments by lot area within two hundred feet of the sewer centerline.

headings.title: Special tax bills, liens, installments, interest, and acceleration
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, history notes, and cross-reference notes. Covers issuing special tax bills as statutory liens on lots or portions within two hundred feet of the sewer centerline, landowner option within twenty days of ordinance/order to request up to five annual installments, 6% interest until due and 10% after default, and acceleration of all unpaid installments with lien enforcement after six months' delinquency.

headings.title: Authentication, engineering costs, and contractor payment by bills
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3, history notes, and cross-reference notes. Covers board or city authentication of tax bills, adding engineering and superintendence costs (capped at 10% of estimated construction cost) to assessments when built by trustees or a county commission versus municipal assumption when built by a city, town, or village, and issuing special tax bills to contractors or suppliers as the exclusive method of payment.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (3 subsections), history notes, and 140.380/249.710–249.750 cross-references; verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked <=1,000-acre subdistrict jurisdiction split (248.070 trustees across independent jurisdictions vs. single municipality/county), majority taxpayer petition or board of health trigger, and 200-foot area-based special assessment in (1), special tax bill liens, 20-day request for <=5 annual installments, 6%/10% interest, and 6-month default acceleration in (2), and authentication, <=10% engineering/superintendence cost allocation (assessed for trustees/county vs. borne by municipality), and exclusive contractor payment in tax bills in (3). Retained all three drafted headings.
